issues.legal_issue: Export duty and sales tax are not deductible from the selling price when calculating the pit-mouth sale value of ore for royalty under leases that allow deductions for carriage, freight, and similar delivery charges.
material_facts: The mining leases calculated royalty using the ore’s pit-mouth sale value, determined by subtracting carriage, freight, and other charges usually incurred in conveying and delivering the ore to purchasers.
The lessee sought to deduct export duty from the price of FOB sales and sales tax from the price of FOR sales.
The export duty was payable before shipment, and the lessee was responsible for sales tax on its own turnover.
The Deputy Commissioner disallowed both deductions, and the assessment was upheld by the State Government and the High Court.
issues.conclusion: Neither export duty nor sales tax is deductible under the leases. The assessment was valid, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The lease language permits deductions for carriage, freight, and charges of the same kind incurred in conveying and delivering ore, not every expense connected with a sale. This interpretation is reinforced by Forms 7 and 7-A and Rule 50(1) of Chapter I, Part A of the Mining Manual, which identify deductions such as commission, port charges, freight, handling, and transport. Although export duty had to be paid before shipment so the goods could be placed on board under an FOB sale, it was not an expense for conveying or delivering the ore. Sales tax, payable by the lessee on its own turnover, was likewise not an expense incidental to conveyance or delivery. The judgment refers to Sections 28 and 137 of the Sea Customs Act, 1878, Section 2 and item 7 of the Second Schedule to the Indian Tariff Act, 1934, and Section 4 of the Central Provinces and Berar Sales Tax Act, 1947; it relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: royalty_valuation_challenge and lease_allows_delivery_cost_deductions and (export_duty_claimed or sales_tax_claimed) and taxes_not_delivery_expenses

predicates.royalty_valuation_challenge: A party challenged a royalty assessment calculated using the sale value of extracted ore at the mine site.
predicates.lease_allows_delivery_cost_deductions: The governing lease permits deductions from the sale price for carriage, freight, and similar charges incurred to convey and deliver ore to purchasers.
predicates.export_duty_claimed: The lessee sought to deduct export duty from the sale price of ore sold for delivery aboard a ship.
predicates.sales_tax_claimed: The lessee sought to deduct sales tax payable on its own sales turnover from the sale price of ore.
predicates.taxes_not_delivery_expenses: The claimed taxes were not expenses incurred for conveying or delivering the ore to purchasers.

issues.definition: When a royalty valuation challenge concerns a lease allowing deductions for delivery costs, a claimed tax that is not a delivery expense is disallowed as a deduction from the ore’s sale price.
